simple.meaning: עֲדֶן (ʻăden) is a Hebrew word meaning “till now.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: עֲדֶן (H5728) appears 2 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Ecclesiastes 4:2, with occurrences in Ecclesiastes.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to עֲדֶן (H5728) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in עֲדֶן (H5728) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: עֲדֶן (ʻăden) / H5728 is traced through Ecclesiastes 4:2, Ecclesiastes 4:3 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H5728. aden or adenah עֲדֶ֫נָֿה Eccl 4:2 Baer Ginsb (al. עֲדֶ֫נָּה ), abbreviated עֲדֶן 4:3 ( from עַלהֵֿן עַדהֵֿנָּה, ; compare Late Hebrew עֲדַיִן e. g. Ned. Eccl 9:10 ), adverb hitherto, still.

occurrences.englishText: Therefore I praised the dead who have been long dead more than the living who are yet alive.
Yes, better than them both is him who has not yet been, who has not seen the evil work that is done under the sun.
